newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran paper dismisses UAE naval violation charge.
newsitem.headline: Iran paper dismisses UAE naval violation charge.

text.p: An influential Iranian newspaper on Wednesday rejected charges by the United Arab Emirates that an Iranian navy vessel violated UAE waters when it tried to rescue an Iranian cargo boat.
The daily Iran News, which often reflects the views of Iran's foreign ministry, quoted an "informed source" as saying the incident "was a simple accident."
"Such accidents occasionally happen on both sides of the Persian Gulf and are not considered as an intentional intrusion into other countries' territory," the source said.

The UAE protested to Iran on Tuesday over the incident, saying the naval vessel crossed into UAE territorial waters on January 19 without receiving prior permission in order to tow the small cargo boat.
Relations between the UAE and non-Arab Iran, neighbours across the Gulf, have been strained for years over a territorial dispute concerning three Gulf islands.
In 1992 the UAE accused Iran of occupying the islands of Greater and Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa and revived its territorial claim after Iran tightened security measures at Abu Musa.
The UAE has urged Iran to take the row to the International Court of Justice. Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable and has called for bilateral talks.
